key_insight: Concentrating NACA0006 airfoil-grid flow straighteners near the pipe wall can reduce turbulence enough to produce a net drag reduction, not just a local pressure loss.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical way to improve energy efficiency in long-distance water and gas pipelines by increasing throughput at the same pressure difference.
method: Axisymmetric RANS simulations with the k-ω SST turbulence model and periodic boundary conditions
Validated against fully developed turbulent pipe flow and a prior large-eddy breakup device experiment
Compared concentric-ring grid layouts, especially near-wall placement with 0.5 m axial spacing
evidence_signal: At about Re ≈ 10^5, the near-wall ring grid increased flow rate by up to 9.0%, reduced area-integrated Reynolds shear stress by 29%, and stayed beneficial across 5×10^4 to 2×10^5.
watch_item: The result is model-based rather than direct full-scale pipe testing, so real-world performance may depend on fabrication tolerances, installation losses, and off-design operating conditions.
paper_title: Net drag reduction in turbulent pipe flow by airfoil-section grids concentrated near the wall
